- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackClient (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a5bc8a04783e83cdf4350a4c6ca8e746e7719858` — the merge of head `f407440dd96a697faa6cbb3a7e9f861ba28fbea0` into base `7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a5bc8a04783e83cdf4350a4c6ca8e746e7719858 && git checkout a5bc8a04783e83cdf4350a4c6ca8e746e7719858
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 f407440dd96a697faa6cbb3a7e9f861ba28fbea0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 && git merge --no-ff f407440dd96a697faa6cbb3a7e9f861ba28fbea0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3690b8ef570cce5285675607e29e346b77cb9a73`
Local-runs: none
Scope: skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md, skills/objectstack-ai/evals/skills-tools-knowledge.json + packages/client/src/index.ts, content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx, content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx, .changeset/34189-pending-action-decide-session.md
Security-touching: yes

Read at 2026-11-16T02:14Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6905370348; lane request 6905360702 on mailbox #33873 (the lane's at-tier reviewer was unavailable). Independence: implemented in an os-steve project thread, dispatched by domain:skills#2 (os-steve); reviewed by os-tesla, who neither dispatched nor implemented it.

No prior record on this PR; findings are numbered fresh and continue no earlier id.

### ① Derived judgments

Read against the contract PR #34001 landed (`fa1fb6f4e`): `packages/spec/src/contracts/ai-service.ts`, section "The in-app assistant door: the same rule, its own channel", the docblocks of `IAIService.proposePendingAction` / `approvePendingAction` / `rejectPendingAction`, and the semantic entry `18.in-app-pending-action-decided-by-person.ts`. The diff was read as the head against its merged main parent `b51cb18a7`: 6 files, +53/−9.

- **Who decides.** "Only the person the call ran as approves or rejects the item" (skill, both docs pages, three docblocks) is point 1 of the contract, word for word in substance. "Another user's `ai:approve` does not decide it" is the same point. Holds.
- **Which credential.** "On their signed-in session to the app; an API key or token is refused, even the person's own" is point 2 together with rule 4's last sentence. Holds as far as it goes; it leaves out one refused class the contract names (S2).
- **As whom it runs.** `actions-as-tools.mdx` drops "approve re-runs the same dispatcher" for "approve runs the action as that person with every gate re-checked". That is point 3, and the dropped phrase is the contract's FROM reading. Holds.
- **Second approver.** "A second approver goes through the approvals engine (the `held` outcome)" is point 1's last sentence and the `approvePendingAction` docblock. Holds; its placement in the skill creates a misreading (S1).
- **Listing.** "A client on a token can still list and get" keeps the existing `ai:read` text; the contract puts none of the deciding points on `listPendingActions`. Holds.
- **Refusal code.** No code is quoted for the new refusals. Correct: the contract registers an envelope for the MCP doors only and names none for the in-app decide doors, and no package in this repository serves the decide routes (`git grep pending-actions` over `packages/**` finds the client and the protocol schemas only). The existing "handle the 403" for the `ai:read` / `ai:approve` split is unchanged.
- **Docblock-only.** Every changed line of `packages/client/src/index.ts` is a comment line; no signature, export, route string or statement moved.
- **Eval.** Case 6 matches the file's schema (`id`, `prompt`, `expected_output`, `files`, `assertions.must_contain` / `must_not_contain`, as cases 1 to 5). Its expected output contains all three `must_contain` strings and neither `must_not_contain` string. The prompt asks for the forbidden act on a token, and the expected answer declines it and lists instead, so it tests the taught rule.
- **Other skills and pages.** `git grep` over `skills/**` for pending action, `ai:approve`, `pending_approval`, `enableActionApproval`: only `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md` teaches the queue, and its other two mentions (the skip rule, pitfall 1) say nothing about who decides. Over `content/docs` outside the release-owned and generated trees, only the two pages in this diff teach deciding. No fifth site is left. No link was added or changed.
- **Not derivable here.** The decide doors live in the cloud repository and cloud#4607 is not readable from this seat. Whatever goes beyond the contract text is therefore unconfirmed, which is S3.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/skills` patch and `@objectstack/client` patch: right. Skill wording and docblock text only; the client docblock ships in its declaration file, so the client entry is owed. `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are right on the PR body and the changeset: nothing an author wrote parses differently, and the narrowing itself was declared by #34001. No package is missing: the two docs pages publish with no package.

CI on this head: 72 check-runs, all completed; 60 success, 12 skipped (opt-in and path-gated jobs), none failed, none running.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H.** `skills/**` is on the governed register and the low-risk arm does not apply (`Security-touching: yes`, a client package release in the same PR). This lands on the maintainer's word only. The PR is a draft, correctly.
- **Security-touching: yes.** The changed hunks teach credential, token and permission behaviour: who may decide a pending action and on which credential. This record stays at the rule layer.
- **Landing order (card item 4).** The contract's "When it binds" section says the in-app door runs the earlier queue until its implementing change ships. Every sentence this PR adds is the TO reading, stated without condition. It is true of the contract on main and becomes true of the door only with the cloud release that carries cloud#4607. The maintainer merges in that release window or after it, not before. This seat cannot confirm the state of cloud#4607.
- **Dev open question (name the refusal code later?).** Answer A, leave "refused" with no code. Main states none for these doors.
- **Dev out-of-scope finding (`actions-as-tools.mdx`).** Taken into this PR by the seat's surface widening 6905036822; reviewed above.
- **Tier of authorship.** Authored below the mandated tier under the maintainer's quota ruling, declared in the PR body; this record is the at-tier review that ruling routes to a review seat.
- SQL push-down: no query, join or id materialisation in the diff.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix.

S1 (should-fix) — `skills/objectstack-ai/SKILL.md`, Human-in-the-loop paragraph: the new clause ends "(the `held` outcome)." and the unchanged next sentence begins "Whether *your* action is held is decided entirely by the skip rule above". Before this change "held" there could only mean "queued for approval". Now it follows the named `held` outcome and reads as that outcome, which is false: `held` is a host policy's decision after the person approved, and `actionSkipReason` / `actionRequiresApproval` say nothing about it. Reword the old sentence ("Whether *your* action is queued …") or move the second-approver clause after it.

S2 (should-fix) — the skill, both docs pages and the docblocks name "an API key or token" as refused and stop there. The contract's point 2, the `IAIService` docblocks and the migration entry all name one more refused class in the same breath: an AI identity, and any call that arrives through an AI door; rule 5 adds that the model's own confirmation never counts. A skill is read by an agent, and that clause is the one addressed to its reader. Add it at least to the skill ("…an API key, a token or an AI identity is refused…; the assistant never decides its own item"), and to eval 6's expected output if the wording allows. The headroom covers it (6019 of 6801).

S3 (should-fix) — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`: "Deciding (approve or reject) takes `ai:approve` AND the person's own signed-in session". The contract on main says another user's `ai:approve` does not decide; it does not say the person needs `ai:approve` to decide their own item, and the enforcing door is not in this repository. The sentence asserts a precondition no source on main carries. The card's item 2 asked for this wording, so it is not held against the dev. Before landing, the seat confirms with the cloud lane whether the person's own decision still takes `ai:approve`, and otherwise words it as the skill does ("another user's `ai:approve` does not decide it").

N1 (nit) — `content/docs/ai/actions-as-tools.mdx`, two lines below the changed sentence: "operators expect single-click yes/no". The decider is now the person, not an operator. This answers the seat's hand-off question: change the word.

N2 (nit) — `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`, the unchanged closing comment of the same block: "These methods are for everything that is not a component — server code, jobs, CLIs, tests." For approve and reject that no longer holds, by the comment this PR adds a few lines above. One qualifying clause would do.

N3 (nit) — eval 6 assertions: `must_contain` "list" matches almost any answer, and `must_not_contain` "/approve" fails a correct answer that names the refused route to explain why it is refused. "pendingActions.list" and dropping "/approve" (the method-call string already discriminates) would be tighter.

N4 (nit) — the changeset says the four places "now say what the confirmation rule says" and states the refusals without condition. One clause that the door enforces this from the runtime release that carries the in-app door, not from this package release, would keep a changelog reader from taking it as that release note; the migration entry tells them to look for exactly that note.

Against the card's scenario (an operator script on a token told to approve the queue): the skill, as written, turns that request down and points at listing and at `held`. Nothing it teaches gives an agent, a script or a stored credential a way to decide for the person. It holds against the contract it teaches, with S1 to S3 as the gaps.
